style: Say clearly and warmly, like a friendly train station announcer
lines: Two trains, one railroad, one graph. Change a train's start, departure time or speed, then press Play and watch where they meet.
The strip beside the graph is the railroad turned on its side. Each train sits at the height of its line.
They met. On the graph, that is exactly where the two lines cross.
Same speed, same direction. The gap never shrinks, so the lines never cross. That system has no solution.
Same equation. The two lines sit on top of each other, so every point is a solution.
The equations cross, but at a time when the trains are not both running. On the track, they never meet.
The gap between the trains is the distance between the two lines, straight up and down.
Setting the two equations equal finds the one time when both trains are at the same mile.
This is dispatch. Each ticket sets part of a schedule. You set the rest so the trains do what the ticket asks.
Work out the meeting time and mile first. Then press Play and see if you called it.
Can two straight lines cross twice? Try it, and if you think it can't be done, say so.
Drag the round dot to move a departure. Drag the square to change the speed.
Locked settings come from the ticket. Change the others, then press Check.
